2982.T AD Works Group Co., Ltd. 🌐
MI2 Corporation, Murakami Takateru, and MI5 Corporation reported a joint 10.77% stake in AD Works Group Co., Ltd. (2982.T), up from 9.74%. Murakami Takateru controls 8.17%, while MI2 Corporation has pledged 1,174,200 shares, or 90% of its position, as collateral for margin trading with SBI Securities. The filing proposes capital policy changes, specifically higher dividends and share buybacks, and indicates the group may increase its stake beyond 5% within three months or divest depending on price. The filing is the Japanese equivalent of a US 13D with an activist agenda focused on capital returns. AD Works can address the demand with its JPY2.2B (~$14M) in self-funding, but the 90% collateralization of MI2's position creates a structural overhang because margin calls could force the sale of nearly 2.6% of the float.

8929.T Aoyama Zaisan Networks Co., Ltd. 🌐
Asset Value Investors Limited (AVI) filed a large shareholding report on June 9, 2026, disclosing a 7.18% stake in Aoyama Zaisan Networks Co., Ltd. (8929.T). The UK-based investment manager holds 1,803,790 shares at a total acquisition cost of approximately ¥2.94 billion (~$18M), though the position decreased from a prior 8.21% following off-market sales at ¥1,315. Although the filing cites a pure investment purpose, AVI reserved the right to push for director appointments or removals, board composition changes, asset disposals, and capital policy shifts. AVI has engaged the Tokyo-based Iwata Law Office as its local contact for engagement with the $195M market-cap real estate firm. This filing is the Japanese equivalent of a US 13D with a public agenda and creates a new activist vector where AVI’s prior 8.21% stake had been passive.

ASH Ashland Inc.
Ancora Holdings Group has publicly demanded that Ashland Inc. (ASH) pursue a full-company sale, estimating a potential valuation of approximately $76 per share. This entry marks a shift from the cooperative approach of Standard Investments, which currently holds a ~10% stake in the specialty chemicals company. Ancora has signaled a willingness to launch a proxy contest in September if its demands are not met. Ashland recently appointed Bertrand Loy to its board effective May 15, while Seaport Global Securities upgraded the stock to Buy with a $75 target. This campaign introduces a control catalyst with an estimated 19% upside to the $63.61 share price, requiring PMs to track the September nomination window as the next escalation checkpoint.

CHE Chemed Corporation
Barington Capital Group has established a significant equity stake in Chemed Corporation (CHE) and is engaging management regarding potential board changes. DSX Diana Shipping Inc. 🌐
Diana Shipping Inc. (DSX) is focusing its proxy campaign at Genco Shipping & Trading Limited on the election of Jens Ismar and Paul Cornell at Genco's June 18, 2026 annual meeting. Diana, advised by Okapi Partners, is urging shareholders to vote for Ismar and Cornell, withhold votes from Genco nominees Basil G. Mavroleon and Arthur L. DRVN Driven Brands Holdings Inc. ✓ live实时
ADW Capital Management, which beneficially owns 4.8% of Driven Brands Holdings Inc. (DRVN) via stock and options, issued a public letter demanding the board undertake a strategic review. The activist disclosed an $18.00 per share offer for the automotive aftermarket service franchisor, in which Roark Capital Group owns over 60%. ADW alleges Roark faces LP pressure in its 2012 Fund III and 2016 Fund IV and is prioritizing an Inspire Brands IPO over monetizing DRVN while earning management fees on $34B AUM. Driven Brands has seen double-digit year-to-date share price declines and is not current on financials while suffering from ballooning corporate SG&A despite divesting a major business. The activist is attacking the GP's LP-level incentives as a pressure vector to force the sponsor-controlled name into play as fund vintages age past years 12 to 15. Any board response or strategic review launch is the next catalyst for testing the $18.00 per share takeout floor.

FRMI Fermi Inc. ✓ live实时
Fermi Inc. (FRMI) is facing a consent solicitation from former CEO Toby Neugebauer to call a special shareholder meeting for the purpose of expanding the board by seven nominees. Neugebauer, who was terminated for cause on April 30, 2026, controls 22.7% of common stock, with an aggregate ownership of approximately 40.3% including family and existing board designees. The Neugebauer Group seeks to seat nominees to evaluate a sale, joint venture, or standalone strategy, while Fermi’s independent committee has engaged Innisfree M&A Incorporated to solicit the revocation of agent designations. This contest features an exceptionally high 40.3% starting ownership stake that will test whether the independent board can hold the line on its strategic review versus Neugebauer’s push for an immediate sale. The consent bar under Texas law and a May 13 supermajority bylaw amendment are likely the key battlefronts for this control contest.

4189.T KH Neochem Co., Ltd. 🌐
Strategic Capital Inc. reported an increased 17.08% stake in KH Neochem Co., Ltd. (4189.T), totaling 6,344,600 shares as of June 1, 2026. The activist accumulated the position via daily market and off-market transactions beginning April 3, 2026, with the filing declaring a purpose of making proposals to increase leverage, reduce equity, and divest or discontinue the basic chemicals business. Nearly all shares are held under a discretionary investment management agreement with Intertrust Trustees (Cayman) Limited, and 900,000 shares are subject to collateral pledges or lending agreements with Tachibana Securities. Skillsoft Corp. (SKIL) entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Global Knowledge instructor-led training business to an affiliate of private equity firm Enduring Ventures for up to $10 million plus additional deferred payments. The transaction includes a strategic partnership for cross-access to content and classifies the unit as discontinued operations, which the company expects to be immediately accretive to growth rates, earnings, and cash flow. Wingtech Technology Co., Ltd. (600745.SS) announced that a dispute regarding the sale of its India business asset package to Luxshare Precision Industry Co., Ltd. and Luxshare Communication (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. has escalated to formal arbitration. The divestiture, originally agreed upon in 2025 to exit Wingtech's ODM manufacturing operations, included several China, Hong Kong, and India subsidiaries. While all other asset packages have successfully completed ownership transfer, the India business package is now subject to Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) proceedings. ABF.L Associated British Foods 🌐
Associated British Foods (ABF.L) is proceeding with the demerger of Primark into a standalone FTSE 100 retailer with an expected completion by the end of 2027. Primark appointed Lucy Slinger as CFO, completing a standalone C-suite that includes CEO Eoin Tonge and CCO Filip Ekvall. Following the separation, AB Foods shareholders will receive shares in both entities, and Wittington Investments will retain control of both companies. The appointment of a CFO serves as the final leadership milestone ahead of the spin-off, which aims to create a pure-play retailer that may re-rate against the conglomerate discount currently embedded in AB Foods.

0836.HK China Resources Power Holdings Company Limited 🌐
China Resources Power Holdings Company Limited (0836.HK) published the full A-share prospectus for the spin-off and Shenzhen Stock Exchange main board IPO of its subsidiary, China Resources New Energy. The offering comprises 2,107,255,000 new shares, representing 16.2% of enlarged capital, or up to 2,423,343,000 shares and 18.19% of capital with full over-allotment. The parent company will retain an 83.80% to 81.81% stake in the SpinCo, which maintains 27.6 GW of wind and 14.0 GW of photovoltaic capacity across 31 Chinese provinces. The RMB 24.5B in proceeds is earmarked for renewable energy base, multi-energy complementarity, and integrated development projects. The Shenzhen listing unlocks a separate valuation for the ~42 GW renewables portfolio, with the 16% to 18% free float creating a substantial equity raise to be priced against Chinese clean-energy comparables.

SCLX Scilex Holding Company
Scilex Holding Company (SCLX) confirmed the June 15, 2026, payment date for its pro-rata dividend of Semnur Pharmaceuticals (OTC: SMNR) common stock. Shareholders of record as of June 1, 2026, will receive one share of Semnur for each share of Scilex common stock held. Semnur is a clinical late-stage specialty pharmaceutical company developing SP-102 (SEMDEXA), a non-opioid gel formulation for epidural injections to treat sciatica, with a completed Phase 3 study and FDA Fast Track status. Nasdaq has set the ex-dividend date for the distribution as June 16, 2026, and Scilex will retain majority ownership of Semnur post-distribution. The confirmed dates lock in the timetable for the distribution, which uses SPAC-like mechanics to create a tradable stub in a late-stage biotech asset with a completed Phase 3 trial and Fast Track designation for sciatica.

TKA.DE Thyssenkrupp AG 🌐
Thyssenkrupp AG (TKA.DE) rebranded its Materials Services division as TK Accelis as management targets a full spin-off of the unit before the end of 2026. The division generated EUR 11.4B (~$13.2B) in revenue during fiscal year 2024/25 and employs approximately 15,500 people. The group recently finalized its exit from the AST stainless-steel plant, selling its remaining 15% stake to Arvedi for a high-double-digit-million-euro cash inflow. Shares fell 3.53% on Wednesday and trade 21% below the 52-week high of EUR 13.24 (~$15) amid steel-division capacity cuts and a labor rally scheduled for Friday. The rebranding converts the long-telegraphed restructuring theme into a dated catalyst for a year-end spin-off of the EUR 11.4B (~$13.2B)-revenue division. The upcoming mid-June 2026 supervisory board meeting is the next checkpoint for concrete terms as the AST exit removes a legacy overhang.

VEDL.NS Vedanta Limited 🌐
Vedanta Limited (VEDL.NS) will complete a four-way demerger as Vedanta Aluminium Metal, Vedanta Oil & Gas, Vedanta Power, and Vedanta Iron & Steel list on the BSE and NSE on June 15. Shareholders receive one share of each spin-off entity per Vedanta share held on the May 1 record date, while Vedanta Limited retains the Hindustan Zinc, copper, and critical minerals businesses. Vedanta Oil & Gas is targeting 300,000 to 500,000 bpd production with a $5 billion investment plan, and Vedanta Power operates 4.2 GW of capacity with a 12 GW expansion pipeline. The start of trading ends the price-discovery gap persisting since the May record date. First market pricing of the four spun-off units will reveal whether the demerger unlocks value as intended, while placement in the T2T segment mandates compulsory delivery and precludes short-term speculative volume.

1171.HK Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited 🌐
Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited (1171.HK) is seeking shareholder approval to spin off its 45%-held subsidiary, Wubo Technology, for a separate listing on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. ARCpoint Inc. (ARC.V) appointed Peter Kendall as Interim CEO for a 90-day term to conduct a formal assessment of the company’s business model, MAPL platform, and strategic direction. Kendall is tasked with providing the board a recommendation on the commercial path forward following the transition of former CEO John Constantine to a sales and marketing role. Compensation for the interim role includes 4,000,000 RSUs vesting over 12 months, with a non-continuance fee of C$20,000 (~$14.3K) or 2,000,000 RSUs if no ongoing engagement is established. The review covers the entire business of the TSX Venture Exchange-listed healthcare technology provider. This board-initiated strategic review creates a binary catalyst where the 90-day mandate will result in a recommendation ranging from a potential sale of the company to a pivot or wind-down.

BNED Barnes & Noble Education
Barnes & Noble Education (BNED) disclosed in its May 30, 2026, Form 10-Q substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern over the next 12 months. The board of directors has initiated a strategic review of alternatives including asset sales, new financing, restructuring, or a sale of the entire company. For the quarter ended January 25, 2026, the company reported a net loss and negative operating cash flow driven by soft textbook sales and digital investment costs. Management has provided no timeline for the review and stated there is no guarantee that any transaction will result from the process. This disclosure creates a binary setup for equity holders where a successful sale or recapitalization could re-rate the stock, while a distressed capital raise would likely dilute or wipe out common equity.

BHR Braemar Hotels & Resorts Inc.
Braemar Hotels & Resorts Inc. (BHR) concluded its strategic review on June 12, 2026, with the independent Special Committee recommending against a company sale and opting instead to transition to a self-managed REIT. The company will terminate its advisory agreement with Ashford Inc., a move expected to generate more than $25M in annual G&A cost savings. To fund termination fees owed to Ashford, Braemar plans to sell two to three additional hotel assets, retaining a focused portfolio of six to eight luxury properties. The board will undergo a near-total reconstitution, naming five new independent directors while all current directors except CEO Richard Stockton resign. Robert W. Baird & Co. Inc. served as financial advisor and White & Case LLP as legal counsel for the review. The self-management internalization and projected cost savings create a tangible value-unlock thesis while the board refresh and Ashford separation remove a long-standing external-manager overhang.

GPRO GoPro, Inc.
GoPro, Inc. (GPRO) disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern in a June 1, 2026, Form 8-K filing. The company is actively seeking a buyer following an April 2026 press release and verbal support from its CEO for a sale process. GoPro has executed two rounds of 25% workforce reductions in November 2024 and April 2026. Credit agreements with Farallon Capital, Wells Fargo, and YA II PN contain restrictive covenants that may limit the company's ability to raise additional capital. The ITC ruled in GoPro's favor on a single design patent against Insta360 but dismissed or ruled against its technology patent claims. This going-concern warning formalizes the distress behind GoPro's strategic-sale process and signals a lack of runway, with restrictive financing covenants making a sale or merger the most likely path for potential acquirers negotiating from a position of strength.
